card: Subclasses Python's HTTPConnection in the functional test framework to enforce ephemeral port ranges before establishing connections. On FreeBSD and OpenBSD, default ephemeral port ranges overlap with test ports, causing http.client sockets to occasionally assign identical source and destination ports and connect to themselves when targeting closed ports. The author encountered this while stress-testing native FreeBSD CI in #36147, where a wrong-RPC-port startup check failed with BadStatusLine after reading its own request. This PR unblocks reliable BSD functional test runs in #36147.
evidence: PR description: 'While stress-testing #36147 I noticed sporadic port collisions still occurring on FreeBSD... For example, the wrong-RPC-port startup check failed with BadStatusLine: POST / HTTP/1.1 because the client read back its own request.'
problem: On BSD systems, default ephemeral port allocations overlap with the test framework's fixed port range. Because Python's internal http.client handles its own socket creation, it bypasses set_ephemeral_port_range(), allowing outgoing RPC or REST calls to closed ports to select identical source and destination ports and connect to themselves.

risk.why: A mistake can only cause functional test failures during RPC or REST client connections, primarily on BSD systems.

scope_notes: Small functional test framework change replacing standard HTTP connections with a subclass in netutil across AuthServiceProxy and direct HTTP test calls.
summary: Subclasses Python's HTTPConnection in the functional test framework to configure ephemeral port ranges before connecting. It routes test RPC and direct HTTP requests through this subclass on FreeBSD and OpenBSD to prevent client sockets from self-connecting to closed ports.
